- Refactor MCP tools into modular structure with separate files by category:
  - `queue.py`: Queue-related tools (read-only)
  - `field.py`: Global field and metadata tools (read-only)
  - `issue_read.py`: Issue read-only tools
  - `issue_write.py`: Issue write tools (conditional on read-only mode)
  - `user.py`: User-related tools (read-only)

def register_board_tools(settings: Settings, mcp: FastMCP[Any]) -> None:
    """Register board and sprint tools (all read-only)."""

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get All Boards",
        description="Get the agile boards (in russian - 'доски') available in Yandex Tracker. "
        "Use the returned board id with the `board_get`, `board_get_columns` and "
        "`board_get_sprints` tools. "
        "Pass `queue` to get only the boards that collect issues of that queue - "
        "that is the way to answer 'which board does this project use'. It matches "
        "the board's own filter, so it misses boards filtering by something else "
        "(personal boards, for one); to catch those, read a few issues of the queue "
        "with `issues_find` and look at their `boards` field. "
        "An organization can have hundreds of boards, so the listing is paginated: "
        "it returns a page of boards plus `next_cursor`, which you pass back as "
        "`cursor` to get the next one until it comes back null. Pass `fields` to "
        "keep the answer small while searching for the board you need. "
        "Boards are organization-wide and are NOT filtered by the server's queue "
        "allow-list: a board's settings can name a queue this server otherwise "
        "refuses to talk about.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def boards_get_all(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        queue: BoardQueueFilter = None,
        fields: BoardFieldsParam = None,
        cursor: BoardCursorParam = None,
        per_page: CursorPerPageParam = 25,
    ) -> BoardsPage:
        if queue is not None:
            check_queue_access(settings, queue)

        boards_api = ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards
        auth = get_yandex_auth(ctx)

        if queue is None:
            boards = await boards_api.boards_list(
                per_page=per_page, cursor=cursor, auth=auth
            )
            # `_paginate` sorts by id ascending, so the id of the last board is
            # the cursor for the next page; a short page means there is none.
            next_cursor = boards[-1].id if len(boards) == per_page and boards else None
        else:
            # Tracker offers no server-side filter here - a board has no queue
            # field, it is matched by the queue in its own auto-filter - so a
            # match can be anywhere and the listing has to be walked. Walking it
            # a page at a time rather than asking for all of it at once is what
            # keeps every request the same size whatever the organization: the
            # unpaged endpoint is one request that grows without bound, and no
            # timeout covers both a small Tracker and a large one.
            # `board_queue_keys` upper-cases what it reads, so the match ignores
            # case the way the allow-list check does.
            wanted = queue.upper()
            boards = []
            next_cursor = cursor
            while len(boards) < per_page:
                batch = await boards_api.boards_list(
                    per_page=BOARDS_SCAN_PAGE, cursor=next_cursor, auth=auth
                )
                boards.extend(b for b in batch if wanted in board_queue_keys(b))
                if len(batch) < BOARDS_SCAN_PAGE:
                    # Short page: the listing is exhausted, so there is nothing
                    # left to continue from however few matches were found.
                    next_cursor = None
                    break
                # The cursor follows the boards examined, not the ones matched,
                # or continuing would rescan everything between two matches.
                next_cursor = batch[-1].id

        if fields is not None:
            set_non_needed_fields_null(boards, {f.name for f in fields})

        return BoardsPage(boards=boards, next_cursor=next_cursor)

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get Board",
        description="Get a single Yandex Tracker agile board (in russian - 'доска') "
        "with its settings. `autoFilterSettings` is the board's own filter and tells "
        "which issues the board collects - read it to learn which queue a board is about. "
        "Also returns the columns, the field issues are estimated by and the working "
        "calendar the board uses.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def board_get(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        board_id: BoardID,
        fields: BoardFieldsParam = None,
    ) -> Board:
        board = await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.board_get(
            board_id,
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

        if fields is not None:
            set_non_needed_fields_null([board], {f.name for f in fields})

        return board

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get Board Columns",
        description="Get the columns of a Yandex Tracker agile board together with the "
        "issue statuses mapped onto each of them. Use it to find out which status an "
        "issue has to be in to show up in a given column of the board. "
        "Richer than the columns nested in `boards_get_all` / `board_get`, which carry "
        "no statuses.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def board_get_columns(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        board_id: BoardID,
    ) -> list[BoardColumnDetail]:
        return await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.board_get_columns(
            board_id,
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Get Board Sprints",
        description="Get all sprints (in russian - 'спринты') of a specific Yandex Tracker agile board. "
        "The currently running sprint is the one with status 'in_progress'. "
        "Use the returned sprint id to put an issue into a sprint "
        "with the `issue_create` or `issue_update` tools.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=True),
    )
    async def board_get_sprints(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        board_id: BoardID,
        fields: SprintFieldsParam = None,
    ) -> list[Sprint]:
        sprints = await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.boards.board_get_sprints(
            board_id,
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

        if fields is not None:
            set_non_needed_fields_null(sprints, {f.name for f in fields})

        return sprints

    fix: match the queue allow-lists ignoring case, from a set
    
    `is_queue_allowed` and `_is_read_only_queue` compared a queue key to the
    configured list exactly, and nothing upper-cased either side: Tracker's
    keys are upper-case, the environment variables are written by hand. A
    mis-cased entry therefore did not fail, it quietly meant something else -
    `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES=dev` locked out `DEV-1` along with every other
    queue, and `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES=dev` left `DEV` writable while the
    configuration read as if it were protected.
    
    Normalising per comparison would have cost a pass over the list every
    time, and `is_queue_allowed` is what a listing tool runs per row. So it
    happens once instead: `decode_queue_keys` (was `decode_numbers`, which
    parsed no numbers) returns a `set[str]` of upper-cased keys for both
    variables, and a check is `queue.upper() in ...`. The validator takes a
    list, set or tuple as well as the raw string, so a programmatic caller is
    normalised the same way and entries differing only in case collapse.
    
    `create_test_settings` builds settings with `model_construct`, which
    skips validators - it calls `decode_queue_keys` itself now, or the tests
    would assert the case-insensitivity against raw lists that never went
    through it.

# Funnel every Tracker request through one `_request()` helper

## Context

`TrackerAPITimeout` landed with the board tools, but it is raised from exactly one place —
`boards_list` (`mcp_tracker/tracker/custom/client.py:2679`) wraps its own `try/except TimeoutError`.
The other 59 aiohttp call sites in that file let a bare `TimeoutError` through, and
`str(TimeoutError())` is the empty string, so a slow endpoint still reaches an agent as
`Error executing tool <name>:` with nothing after the colon.

Per-call-site error handling is exactly the drift AGENTS.md already warns about for the 404 errors
("a dedicated error applies to *every* method scoped to that entity, not just to newly added ones").
Today each of the 60 blocks repeats `headers=await self._build_headers(auth)`,
`await self._raise_for_status(response)` and — 27 times — a hand-written `if response.status == 404`.
A new method is one forgotten line away from any of them.

Outcome: one funnel that every request goes through, so the timeout message, the API's own error text
and the status→domain-error mapping are structural instead of a habit.

## Design

Two helpers on `TrackerClient`, placed next to `_raise_for_status` (~`client.py:355`):

```python
@asynccontextmanager
async def _request(
    self,
    method: str,
    url: str,
    *,
    auth: YandexAuth | None,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    json: Any = None,
    not_found: YandexTrackerError | None = None,
    conflict: YandexTrackerError | None = None,
    allow_statuses: Collection[int] = (),
) -> AsyncIterator[ClientResponse]:
    # Built before the `try`: a service-account IAM fetch stalling is not an
    # API timeout and must not be reported as one.
    headers = await self._build_headers(auth)
    try:
        async with self._session.request(
            method, url, headers=headers, params=params, json=json
        ) as response:
            if response.status not in allow_statuses:
                if not_found is not None and response.status == 404:
                    raise not_found
                if conflict is not None and response.status == 409:
                    raise conflict
                await self._raise_for_status(response)
            yield response
    except TimeoutError as exc:
        raise TrackerAPITimeout(method=method, url=url, timeout=self._timeout) from exc


async def _read(self, method: str, url: str, *, auth, params=None, json=None,
                not_found=None, conflict=None) -> bytes:
    """The body of a request whose caller needs nothing else from the response."""
    async with self._request(...same kwargs...) as response:
        return await response.read()
```

Notes that decide the shape:

- **`self._session.request(method, url, ...)`** rather than `.get`/`.post`. aioresponses patches
  `aiohttp.client.ClientSession._request`, which `request()` delegates to, so every existing mock in
  `tests/` keeps matching without a change.
- **A timeout while reading the body is covered too.** `await response.read()` runs in the caller's
  `async with` block; `@asynccontextmanager` throws that exception into the generator at the `yield`,
  where the same `except TimeoutError` catches it. This is not obvious and gets its own test.
- **`_read` is spelled out, not `**kwargs`** — mypy and `ty` both run in `task check`, and `**kwargs: Any`
  would stop checking the keyword names at ~45 call sites.
- **`allow_statuses`** exists for the single site that wants the raw status: `user_get`
  (`client.py:967`) returns `None` on 404 rather than raising.
- `not_found` / `conflict` take a ready exception instance (`IssueNotFound(issue_id)`), constructed
  eagerly at the call. Negligible cost, and it keeps the call site readable.

## Migration — all 60 call sites in `client.py`

| Shape (count) | Becomes |
|---|---|
| 404→`XNotFound` + parse body (22) | `Model.model_validate_json(await self._read("GET", url, auth=auth, not_found=XNotFound(id)))` |
| plain + parse body (10) | same, without `not_found` |
| plain + `return await response.read()` — the `_entity_*` helpers (10) | `return await self._read(...)` |
| 404→`XNotFound` + `return None` (3) and plain + `return None` (2) | `await self._read(...)`, discard |
| needs the response object (`_paginated`, `_parse_next_cursor`, `.text()`) (13) | `async with self._request(...) as response:` |

Sites that are not mechanical:

- `client.py:544`, `585` (template listings): conditional 404 →
  `not_found=QueueNotFound(queue) if queue is not None else None`.
- `client.py:967` `user_get`: `allow_statuses=(404,)`, keeps `if response.status == 404: return None`.
- `client.py:1261` `issue_update`: `not_found=IssueNotFound(issue_id)`, `conflict=IssueVersionConflict(issue_id, version)`.
- `client.py:999` `issues_count`: keeps `_request` — it reads `int(await response.text())`, and `int(b"5")` is a `TypeError`.
- `client.py:477`, `1265`: keep the existing `params=params if params else None` expression as written, to avoid any URL-matching drift in the mocks.
- `client.py:2679` `boards_list`: drops its own `try/except TimeoutError`; the docstring's paragraph about
  the budget stays, the comment about `str(TimeoutError())` moves into `_request`.
- `client.py:2721` `board_get_sprints`: keeps its comment about a non-scrum board answering 400.

Imports to add: `contextlib.asynccontextmanager`, `collections.abc.{AsyncIterator, Collection, Mapping}`,
`YandexTrackerError` from `mcp_tracker.tracker.custom.errors`.

Manual check when done: `grep -c 'self._session\.' client.py` is 1 — the call inside `_request`.
(No test asserts this; that was ruled out as overkill.)

## Docs

- **`AGENTS.md:44`** — the "Errors" bullet under *Writing to the Tracker API* currently tells an agent to
  call `await self._raise_for_status(response)` per method. Rewrite it around the funnel: every method
  goes through `self._request()` / `self._read()`, a status with an actionable meaning is passed as
  `not_found=` / `conflict=`, and nothing calls `self._session` directly.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`, `[0.8.1-dev]`** — the `TrackerAPITimeout` bullet says the error exists; it now has to
  say it covers every Tracker request, not just the boards listing. Add an *Internal* bullet for the funnel
  (one `_request()` context manager doing headers, timeout translation, `_raise_for_status` and the
  status→error mapping for all 60 call sites).

## Tests

New `tests/tracker/custom/test_request.py`, exercising the funnel itself through a real `TrackerClient`
with `aioresponses` (same fixture style as `tests/tracker/custom/boards/conftest.py`):

- forwards method, url, params and `json` body, and sends the `_build_headers` result (auth + org header)
- `TimeoutError` on the request → `TrackerAPITimeout` naming method, url, the timeout value and `TRACKER_API_TIMEOUT`; message is non-empty
- `TimeoutError` raised while the caller reads the body → the same translation
- 404 with `not_found=` → that error; 404 without it → `TrackerAPIError` carrying Tracker's `errorMessages`
- 409 with `conflict=` → that error; 409 without it → `TrackerAPIError`
- `allow_statuses=(404,)` → the response is yielded, nothing raised
- `_read` returns the raw body bytes and inherits all of the above
- parametrized over `GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE` where the case repeats

The 868 existing tests are what proves the migrated methods still behave — their aioresponses mocks are
untouched by the refactor, so a wrong url, verb, param or missing header fails them. The existing
`tests/tracker/custom/boards/test_boards_list.py::TestBoardsListTimeout` stays as the end-to-end case.

## Verification

1. `task` — lock, format, ruff, mypy, `ty`, pytest (868 + new).
2. During migration, `uv run pytest tests/tracker/custom -q` after each block of methods; it is the layer
   that mocks HTTP and will catch a mistyped url or verb immediately.
3. `uv run pytest tests/mcp -q` last — the tool layer surfaces the errors an agent actually sees.
4. Smoke check against the live Tracker with the `yt-local` MCP tools (`issue_get` on a real key, and a
   deliberately missing key to see `IssueNotFound` rather than a bare 404).
